# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Age:** Teenager (approximately 11–16 throughout the novel)
- **Gender:** Female
- **Status:** Alive
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, Canada
- **Role:** Student, schoolteacher

## Appearance

Ruby is considered one of the prettiest girls in Avonlea, renowned for her fair complexion and long, beautiful golden hair. She has bright blue eyes and a plump, attractive figure. She takes great pride in her looks and her stylish appearance.

## Personality

Ruby is sentimental, giggly, and deeply preoccupied with romance and young men. Though somewhat shallow and prone to weeping at emotional moments, she is sweet-tempered and good-natured. She values fashion, social gossip, and the attentions of suitors above intellectual pursuits, though she remains a loyal friend.

## Traits

- Vain about her looks
- Sentimental and easily moved to tears
- Preoccupied with romance and beaux
- Good-natured and cheerful

## Abilities

- Passing the Queen's Academy entrance examinations
- Earning a teacher's license

## Goals

- To acquire many beaux and eventually marry well
- To successfully pass her examinations at Queen's Academy

## History

Ruby Gillis is one of Anne Shirley's primary schoolmates in Avonlea. She becomes a member of Anne's close circle of friends and joins her Story Club, contributing melodramatic tales about romance. As she grows older, Ruby becomes famous among her peers for having the most suitors and constantly discussing boys. She joins Mr. Phillips's advanced class to prepare for the Queen's Academy entrance exams alongside Anne, Gilbert Blythe, Diana Barry, Jane Andrews, and Josie Pye. After spending a year studying in Charlottetown at Queen's, she successfully obtains her teacher's license and prepares to teach at a local school.

## Background by volume

- Grew up as part of the large Gillis family in Avonlea
- Attended Avonlea School alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry

## Affiliations

- Avonlea School — Student
- The Story Club — Member
- Queen's Academy — Student
